title: Enterprise Search vs Search-to-Action: 7 Tools for Regulated Industries
summary: Finding a document is step one of a thirty-step KYC or loan workflow. Most search tools stop there. This rubric ranks seven platforms on whether they can govern what happens next.
body_markdown:
### Summary


- Regulated firms need more than generic SaaS search: indexing can expose PII/PHI, vector embeddings can be inverted, and Gartner projects 75% digital sovereignty by 2030.
- Compliance-grade search requires verifiable, citable answers plus on-premise or private cloud deployment, RBAC, SSO, and immutable audit logs.
- Search alone is not enough: KYC, loan, and contract workflows often have 30–40 steps, so platforms must move from retrieval to governed, auditable action.
- For teams that need that execution layer,[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) turns search results into deterministic workflows with audit trails and a 15–60x cost advantage over stochastic agents.


Banks, insurers, and legal firms face an information retrieval problem that generic search tools are not built to solve. Finding a document across Slack, SharePoint, a core banking system, and a legacy case management platform is difficult. Doing so in a way that satisfies a compliance audit, respects granular access controls, and leaves a complete paper trail presents a distinct engineering challenge.


Most SaaS enterprise search platforms do not meet this requirement. During the indexing phase,[cleartext PII and PHI pass through vendor infrastructure](https://www.atolio.com/blog/self-hosted-enterprise-search-vs-saas) regardless of downstream encryption. As Atolio explains, even storing vector embeddings does not resolve the exposure: a 2023 research paper demonstrated that vector representations can be inverted to recover substantial source text, making "we only store vectors" an insufficient security position for regulated workloads.[Gartner projects](https://www.atolio.com/blog/self-hosted-enterprise-search-vs-saas) that more than 75% of enterprises will have a digital sovereignty strategy by 2030. A cloud-only platform is already a procurement obstacle for most regulated buyers.


A second gap is as consequential as security. Enterprise search tools find answers; those answers still require action. In a KYC workflow, a loan review, or a contract check, locating the right document is step one of a thirty-step process.[The limitation is well-documented](https://dust.tt/blog/enterprise-ai-search) : search finds answers but does not execute the work that follows. For regulated enterprises, that gap creates compliance risk and operational cost at the same time.


The seven platforms below are evaluated against a consistent[five-point rubric](https://certant.ai/blog/best-glean-alternatives-regulated-firms) : NLP capability and verifiability, security and compliance posture, deployment options, integration breadth, and the ability to move from retrieved information into governed action.


---


## The Evaluation Rubric


The criteria define the evaluation. Regulated industry buyers need to assess AI-driven enterprise search solutions across five dimensions:


1. NLP capability and verifiability: Does the system understand natural language queries accurately, and can it produce citable, traceable answers? Hallucinations are not acceptable when results feed compliance decisions.
2. **Security and compliance posture:** SOC II compliance, granular audit logging, RBAC, SSO, and Active Directory integration are baseline requirements rather than premium features.
3. Deployment options: On-premise, private cloud (customer VPC), and air-gapped deployment must be available. Cloud-only options fail regulated procurement gates.
4. Integration breadth: The platform must connect to the complex combination of legacy and modern systems that defines large enterprise infrastructure.
5. **From search to action:** Does the platform stop at retrieval, or does it support governed, auditable workflow execution on top of the information it finds?


---


## The 7 Best AI Driven Enterprise Search Solutions for Regulated Industries


### 1. Jinba


[Jinba](https://jinba.io/) is a YC-backed, SOC II compliant AI workflow builder purpose-built for regulated enterprises. It addresses a gap that search-only platforms leave open: once regulated teams find the right information, the downstream workflow, whether a KYC check, a loan review, or a compliance sign-off, still has to be executed in an auditable, governed way. Jinba is built around that execution layer.


**NLP capability and verifiability:**[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) uses chat-to-flow generation to translate natural language instructions into deterministic, step-by-step workflows. Every workflow step is logged, producing an immutable audit trail that exceeds the citation-level verifiability of conventional search tools.


**Security and compliance posture:** SOC II compliant. Jinba is engineered for banking and insurance environments with full audit logging, RBAC, SSO, and Active Directory integration built in as standard. Anthropic's documentation confirms that Claude Cowork lacks audit logs and is not suitable for regulated workloads. Jinba is designed for those workloads.


**Deployment options:** On-premise and private cloud deployment are standard offerings, including support for air-gapped environments where data cannot leave the customer's infrastructure. Private model hosting is available via AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, or self-hosted models.


**Integration breadth:** Jinba provides secure connectors and engineering support for integration with core banking processors, internal databases, and enterprise systems. In the US market, a single integration with a core banking processor provides access to 400 to 800 credit unions.


**From search to action:** This is the platform's defining capability.[Jinba Flow](https://flow.jinba.io/) lets technical and semi-technical teams build reusable workflows through a chat interface or a visual editor, publishing them as APIs, batch processes, or MCP servers.[Jinba App](https://app.jinba.io/) provides a safe, chat-based execution environment for non-technical users who run those workflows under RBAC-controlled access. The architecture is 80% deterministic, which means workflow execution does not depend on stochastic LLM inference at every step. At scale, this produces a 15 to 60x cost advantage over stochastic AI agent equivalents: $5 to $20 per month versus $300 or more, a direct response to CFO concerns about[rising enterprise AI spend](https://www.dataart.com/blog/ai-finops-why-your-ai-spend-is-rising-and-how-to-fix-it) .


Jinba's documented deployments include MUFG and Mitsubishi Bank, with approximately 70 enterprise case studies across banking and insurance.


### 2. Sinequa (ChapsVision)


[Sinequa](https://www.chapsvision.com/blog/enterprise-ai-search-compared/) , now part of ChapsVision, is a long-established enterprise search platform with strong neural search capabilities. It is actively repositioning toward agentic AI through its "Chaps Agents" initiative, which ties search retrieval to downstream AI-driven workflow execution.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** Sinequa's neural search engine is well-regarded for relevance and contextual understanding across large, heterogeneous document corpora.


**Security and compliance posture:** Governance and security controls are suited to large enterprise deployments. The platform has an established track record in European regulated sectors.


**Deployment options:** Supports sovereign deployment options, including on-premise and private cloud.


**Integration breadth:** Deep integrations across enterprise content repositories, built over more than two decades in the market.


**From search to action:** Sinequa is building toward this capability. Its agentic AI layer is emerging rather than mature, making it a credible option for enterprises that want a search-first foundation with a roadmap toward governed action.


---


### 3. Certant


[Certant](https://certant.ai/blog/best-glean-alternatives-regulated-firms) is a compliance-first AI-driven enterprise search solution designed specifically for regulated firms. Its defining feature is paragraph-level citation: every statement in a generated answer is traceable to a specific source passage. For legal and compliance teams, this is the difference between a usable answer and a liability.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** Paragraph-level citations make Certant one of the most verifiable options in this category. Answers are grounded in source passages.


**Security and compliance posture:** It is purpose-built for regulated work and places strong emphasis on traceable AI outputs.


**Deployment options:** Cloud, on-premise, and air-gapped deployments are all supported. Certant also supports bring-your-own-model configurations via AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, and local GPUs, giving enterprises full control over the model layer.


**Integration breadth:** The platform is designed to connect across the document-heavy systems common in financial services, healthcare, and government.


**From search to action:** Certant focuses on verifiable retrieval rather than downstream workflow execution. It is the right fit for teams where the compliance requirement is the answer itself, rather than what happens after it.


---


### 4. Elastic Enterprise Search


Elastic Enterprise Search is built on the Elasticsearch engine, giving it best-in-class scalability and flexibility. It is the preferred option for technical teams that want to build a governed search layer on top of their own infrastructure.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** The platform offers strong semantic search capabilities. Verifiable citations typically require custom development on top of the base platform.


**Security and compliance posture:** The platform provides highly configurable RBAC, extensive logging, and broad security tooling. Teams with deep Elastic expertise can achieve compliance-grade configurations.


**Deployment options:** Cloud, on-premise, and hybrid deployments are all available. Self-managed deployment gives enterprises full infrastructure control.


**Integration breadth:** Extensive connector library and a mature API surface, making it adaptable to nearly any enterprise data source.


**From search to action:** Elastic does not provide native workflow execution. It is a search-and-retrieval foundation for teams building their own downstream logic.


---


### 5. Onyx


Onyx is built around data sovereignty. Its architecture assumes the customer controls the full stack, making it a natural fit for enterprises with strict requirements about where data resides and how it is processed.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** Configurable citation options allow teams to calibrate verifiability to their specific regulatory requirements.


**Security and compliance posture:** The platform is architected around data sovereignty principles by design, rather than as an add-on to a cloud-native product.


**Deployment options:** Primarily self-hosted, with cloud options available. The default posture is full customer infrastructure control.


**Integration breadth:** Covers common enterprise knowledge sources with a growing connector set.


**From search to action:** Onyx is focused on retrieval and does not offer native workflow execution capabilities.


---


### 6. Atolio


[Atolio](https://www.atolio.com/blog/self-hosted-enterprise-search-vs-saas) is a self-hosted enterprise search platform with a defence-sector pedigree. It holds a $1.25M US Air Force SBIR contract, which demonstrates that its architecture is trusted in air-gapped, high-security environments where most commercial platforms are not qualified to operate.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** AI-powered search focused on understanding organisational knowledge across internal sources.


**Security and compliance posture:** The Air Force SBIR contract is the most concrete evidence in this category. Atolio runs the entire stack, connectors, index, and models, inside the customer's own infrastructure from day one.


**Deployment options:** Fully self-hosted. No vendor infrastructure touches the customer's data at any stage, including during indexing.


**Integration breadth:** Connectors for common enterprise content sources, with a focus on deployment flexibility over connector breadth.


**From search to action:** Atolio is a retrieval platform. It does not offer downstream workflow capabilities.


---


### 7. Coveo


Coveo is a cloud-native enterprise search platform with a strong relevance engine, most commonly deployed in customer service and e-commerce contexts. It is less suited to regulated industries with strict on-premise requirements.


**NLP capability and verifiability:** Advanced machine learning personalises results effectively. Partial citation capabilities are available.


**Security and compliance posture:** The platform has a strong security posture for cloud environments and is less adapted to on-premise or air-gapped compliance mandates.


**Deployment options:** Primarily cloud-based, with hybrid options. Enterprises with strict data residency or air-gapped requirements will find this a significant constraint.


**Integration breadth:** Broad connector library suited to modern SaaS environments.


**From search to action:** Coveo does not offer native workflow execution. It is best positioned for organisations where cloud deployment is permissible and the primary need is relevance-tuned retrieval.

## Moving from Search to Action


The capability to find information securely across siloed enterprise systems is now a baseline expectation for regulated industries rather than a differentiator. The procurement question has shifted.


The central constraint identified across banking, insurance, and legal operations is whether a platform can support what happens after a document is found: the governed, auditable, repeatable workflow that satisfies both the compliance officer and the operations team. As DataArt's AI FinOps analysis shows, overall enterprise AI spend keeps rising even as per-token costs fall, because stochastic agents consume tokens on every execution. The architecture of the platform matters as much as its search capability.


For teams evaluating air-gapped search with strong verifiability, Certant and Atolio are the clearest options. For teams with sovereignty as the primary requirement and existing technical depth, Elastic and Onyx provide maximum infrastructure control. For enterprises that require governed execution on top of retrieved information, Jinba is the only platform in this list where workflow automation is a core product rather than a roadmap item.


The distinction matters most in high-volume, multi-step processes: KYC document workflows with 30 to 40 component steps, loan underwriting automation, prior authorisation in healthcare, and regulatory compliance checks in pharma. In those contexts, a search result that does not trigger an audited action is an incomplete solution.


---


Organizations can assess where AI workflow automation can replace manual steps in regulated operations. Jinba's consulting team offers a[free AI strategy assessment](https://jinba.io/consulting) backed by approximately 70 enterprise implementations, including MUFG and Mitsubishi Bank. The output is a board-ready plan identifying high-impact automation opportunities specific to the organization's compliance environment.


## Frequently Asked Questions: AI-Driven Enterprise Search for Regulated Industries


### What is AI-driven enterprise search for regulated industries?


AI-driven enterprise search uses natural language processing, semantic search, and retrieval-augmented generation to find and summarise information across an organisation's internal systems. For regulated industries such as banking, insurance, and legal, it must also preserve access controls, provide citable answers, and maintain an auditable trail.


### Why cannot regulated firms rely on generic SaaS enterprise search tools?


Generic SaaS tools often index data in vendor-controlled cloud infrastructure, which can expose cleartext PII and PHI during processing. Regulated firms also need on-premise or private cloud deployment, granular access controls, and audit logs that many cloud-only products do not provide natively.


### What is vector inversion, and why does it matter for PII and PHI?


Vector inversion is a technique researchers use to reconstruct substantial source text from vector embeddings. It matters because storing only embeddings does not fully protect sensitive data; regulated organisations should require search platforms that avoid vendor-side indexing and support full self-hosting.


### What is the difference between on-premise, private cloud, and air-gapped deployment?


On-premise means the platform runs entirely in the customer's data centre; private cloud runs in a customer-controlled VPC; air-gapped means no connection to the internet. Regulated buyers often require at least one of these options to meet data residency and sovereignty mandates.


### How do AI search platforms verify answers for compliance?


Platforms verify answers by grounding responses in source documents and providing citations, sometimes at paragraph level. Some tools also log every step of a workflow so that compliance teams can trace exactly how a result was produced.


### Which enterprise search platforms also support workflow automation?


Most platforms in this article stop at retrieval. Jinba is the only option where governed workflow execution is a core feature, allowing teams to turn retrieved information into repeatable, auditable processes such as KYC checks or loan reviews.


### What are the best Glean alternatives for regulated firms?


The strongest Glean alternatives for regulated firms depend on the requirement. Certant and Atolio offer verifiable, self-hosted search; Sinequa and Elastic provide enterprise-scale retrieval; Jinba combines search with governed workflow automation for teams that require workflow execution in addition to answers.


### How much does AI workflow automation cost compared with stochastic AI agents?


Deterministic workflow automation can cost $5 to $20 per month per user, whereas stochastic AI agents may cost $300 or more. Jinba's 80% deterministic architecture provides a 15 to 60x cost advantage at scale.


### What should compliance teams look for in audit logging and RBAC?


Compliance teams should require immutable audit logs, role-based access control, single sign-on, and Active Directory integration. These controls should be native to the platform rather than sold as a premium feature or left to the customer to build.


### Is Elastic Enterprise Search suitable for regulated firms?


Elastic can be suitable if a team has deep technical expertise and wants maximum scalability. However, citation and workflow execution often require custom development, and the platform does not provide native governed action on top of retrieval.
